role: The server's player roster: login and logout, player NBT save and load, respawn and dimension transfer, the packet broadcasts and the view-distance plumbing.
scope_reason: The single local player's whole server-side life runs through it; world.conf switches none of it (the ban, op and whitelist lists it also owns are never written, so those paths are constants). Deferred: native never writes save files; Java writes every checkpoint (product decision, not a gap for the GPU or the golden chain); tab-list pings are multiplayer; game-type plumbing is survival-only (triage 2026-09-25, out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md).

members.name: respawnPlayer
members.note: the fresh EntityPlayerMP constructor's spawn fuzz draws on every respawn, bed or not; an invalid bed sends S2B 0 (tile.bed.notValid) and leaves no spawn (clonePlayer does not carry it), bed-respawn-s1 and bed-safe-tops-s1; the bed verification (surv_bed_safe_spot), the collision lift, the S07/S05/S1F run and the manager re-add are there; the conquered-End variant is serverreplay_respawn_conquered, with the same bed check (surv_verify_respawn, S2B 0 and no spawn when the bed is gone; end-bed-exit-s1, end-nobed-exit-s1); a death in the Nether or the End leaves that world first and respawns in the overworld (serverreplay_respawn_leave, sr_respawn_depart and sr_respawn_arrive, shared with the conquered variant); setPlayerLocation runs on the net handler whose playerEntity is still the old object, so the old EntityPlayerMP moves to the fresh player's placement: orbs that cached it pull there (sr_respawn_old_moved, respawn-loop-s1); the new EntityPlayerMP's portal state is fresh (clonePlayer(true) keeps only teleportDirection; survival.c surv_server_fresh_state, pfc-portaldeath-s18)

members.name: transferEntityToWorld
members.note: the scaled Nether coordinates and the placeInPortal live in portal.c's portal_transfer_entity; the End spawn-point branch is in the enter path; for a non-player traveller it is serverreplay.c's sr_travel_place (the scaled and clamped setLocationAndAngles, or the End's getEntrancePortalLocation (100, 50, 0) facing 90, 0; the destination's placeInPortal, the End's obsidian platform) inside sr_living_portal_travel / sr_ie_portal_travel. The old world's updateEntityWithOptionalForce(false) at the moved position is not modelled (it acts only where that position's 32-block neighbourhood is loaded). The populations the destination's search runs spawn their drops ahead of the player (sr->in_transfer, portalmake-s1); the placing half (clamp, placeInPortal, spawnEntityInWorld) runs only for an entity alive: a player dead in the End portal is moved but in no world's lists until the respawn (portal.c, serverreplay.c sr_transfer_player, limbo; pfc-deadportal-f347)

notes: Login, respawn, death and dimension transfer are proven by the death and dimension recordings: surv_death-s1 and surv_death-late-s1 (death to respawn), nether-trip-s1 and nether-trip2-s42 (transfer in and out), end-exit-s1 (the conquered-End respawn at spawn). test_portals.c and test_dims.c cover the worldgen side of a transfer. The ban/op/whitelist machinery is a constant in this game, hence the many n/a members rather than missing ones. Closed by lane/idxworld: func_148537_a (the per-dimension broadcast: the S03 every 20th tick) and updateTimeAndWeatherForPlayer's S03 at a respawn and a dimension change are ported (session.c; survival.c surv_server_fresh; serverreplay.c sr_transfer_player) and held by idx-clientview-s1's client clock. The tab list's S38 rotation feeds a list the single-player client never shows; the game type is survival (WorldInfo's record). The disk half is n/a (lane/idxworld): every save this game makes is the oracle's (a checkpoint's save, session.sh's Save and Quit through Java: AGENTS.md 'Playing a full game'), and the native engine reads what it wrote (region.c for the overworld's region files, the snapshot's saved chunks for DIM-1 and DIM1, structures.json, villages.nbt, worldinfo.nbt, player_server.nbt); writing those files natively is the deferred product work of the 2026-09-25 triage (SPEC.md NEXT, '11 deferred save-writing'; out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md, 'Deferred, not noise'). Within a session nothing reads a save back: an unloaded chunk waits whole in the in-memory region store (sr_store_chunk) with what writeChunkToNBT keeps of it (the entities it saves, in section order; the pending ticks relative to the world time), and a reload restores exactly that (the persist-* and play-reload recordings).
